fields.name: Data Platform & Infrastructure
fields.description: Companies building the platforms other engineers run their data on — warehouses, pipelines, observability, streaming and the tooling around them. Roles that sit between platform engineering and product, where the users are themselves technical.
emphasis: Eight years building and running production data platforms, most recently for a team of 60+ internal consumers
Pipeline reliability as a product concern, not a ticket queue: SLOs, lineage, and an on-call rota that shrank rather than grew
Hands-on with dbt, Airflow, Kafka and Snowflake — still writing the code, not only reviewing it
Cost work with a number attached: cut warehouse spend 40% without a drop in query throughput
Migrated a monolithic nightly batch to incremental models, taking the critical path from 6 hours to 35 minutes

fields.name: Developer Advocacy & Technical Enablement
fields.description: Roles where the job is helping other engineers succeed with a technical product — developer relations, solutions engineering, technical enablement and documentation leadership. Suits someone who has done the engineering and would rather teach it.
emphasis: Ran an internal enablement programme that took 40+ analysts from SQL-only to shipping their own dbt models
Conference speaking and workshop delivery — four talks, two of them keynotes at regional meetups
Writes for engineers: a data-engineering blog with a small but real readership, and the internal docs everyone actually cites
Solutions work alongside sales engineers on three enterprise onboardings
Maintains a small open-source dbt package with ~400 GitHub stars
